title: prefill-surge-tactical-scratch
body:
Context / summary:

Quick scratchpad for the weird throughput regression observed on 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-11 where 99th p50 token latency increased and effective qps dropped ~18% on the small GPU pool (gpool-s-4). Suspect interaction between prefill/kv-cache warmup and the continuous-batcher's window heuristics after the config change that reduced max_batch_window_ms from 40 -> 20 as part of PR 2281.

Symptoms observed:
- Ramp at 09:12 UTC: aggregate request rate steady ~850 rps, but served throughput (tokens/s) dips ~15-20% for ~12 minutes then recovers gradually.
- Latency distribution: p50 tokens unchanged, p95 token latency moved from 48ms -> 82ms, p99 from 120ms -> 210ms during the incident window.
- CPU on runtime control plane nodes spikes +30% for the same window, GPU utilization on gpool-s-4 drops slightly (~4-6%) despite more queuing at the scheduler.
- KV cache hit-rate for prefix-only requests dropped from 74% -> 39% in the window; cache eviction spikes aligned with the event.
- Traces show many short-lived prefill tasks concurrently starting, each doing small KV reads then failing to reuse existing warm KV entries.

Key commands / queries I ran (notes + outputs paraphrased):
- kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=batcher --since=30m > batcher-log-snippet.txt
  - saw repeated: "prefill: miss, initiating prefill job id=pf-..." lines approx 1200 occurrences in 12m window

- curl -s "http://metrics.internal/metrics?pool=gpool-s-4&from=2026-02-10T09:00&to=2026-02-10T09:30" | jq '.counters.prefill_initiated'
  - count jumped from baseline ~340 -> 1560 during spike

- pprof cpu profile on batcher (10s) -> go tool pprof -> top shows:
  - runtime/batcher.handleRequest 42%
  - runtime/prefill.startPrefill 28%
  - runtime/cache.EvictIfNeeded 9%

- grep traces for trace ids: tr-9f3c... shows: prefill start -> scan keys -> small set misses -> schedule inference -> after inference, prefill result not stored due to race: "kv.Put failed: write conflict: key-version-mismatch"

Reproduction notes (local-ish):
- Local cluster: run loadgen with high tail-of-stream short requests (avg tokens 8, prefix-heavy). Changing the batcher window to 20ms reproduces similar oscillatory behaviour in the batch queue depth. With 40ms window the system is stable at same RPS.

Observed config diffs around time-of-change: (from deploy manifest history)
- batcher.max_batch_window_ms: 40 -> 20 (PR #2281)
- prefill.concurrent_limit: 24 -> 48 (attempt to accelerate warmups)
- kvcache.eviction_threshold_percent: 85 -> 80

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Shorter max_batch_window_ms reduces time for continuous batcher to accumulate coalesced requests, increasing number of small inference invocations and raising the number of concurrent prefill attempts (since prefill trigger threshold is per-invocation), which amplifies kv cache write contention and eviction churn. Explains higher control-plane CPU and lower effective GPU throughput (more scheduling overhead, smaller kernels).
2) Increasing prefill.concurrent_limit doubled simultaneous prefill writers; combined with lower batch window this increases transient contention on the KV store and leads to more write conflicts. The failed writes lead to misses and subsequent re-prefills (feedback loop).
3) The eviction_threshold drop made cache more aggressive; during high churn this caused hot prefixes to be evicted too quickly, reducing hit rate. Possibly normal but made worse with 1 & 2.
4) A separate regression in KV store commit path (race under high concurrency) — logs show explicit "write conflict: key-version-mismatch" which could be normal compare-and-swap behavior but frequency abnormal.

Evidence for/against each:
- Hypothesis 1: local repro strongly supports. Reverting window to 40ms in canary removes oscillation. Also in traces, number of batches per second increases ~2.1x when window=20ms (same arrival rate).
- Hypothesis 2: logs show prefill concurrency hitting the 48 cap; rolling back to 24 reduces concurrent prefill tasks and improves hit-rate.
- Hypothesis 3: eviction_threshold change is small but correlated; increasing back to 85% restores small part (~4% hit-rate improvement) but not full recovery.
- Hypothesis 4: need deeper KV tracing (enable debug on kv-store-leader). Not yet proven.

Quick mitigations tried (results):
- Revert max_batch_window_ms to 40ms on canary -> throughput recovered, p99 down to baseline. (temporary mitigation)
- Set prefill.concurrent_limit back to 24 only on gpool-s-4 -> hit-rate improved ~18% and fewer write-conflict logs.
- Bumped kvcache.eviction_threshold to 88% (experiment) -> marginal effect.

Longer-term mitigations under consideration:
- Change prefill trigger to be per-prefix (global dedupe) not per-invocation: single prefill job for same prefix queued to a small dedupe queue to avoid N concurrent attempts. (Design doc needed)
- Adjust batcher heuristics: allow adaptive windowing (closed-loop) where window increases under high prefill thrash; or prefer key-owner batching (co-locate requests sharing prefixes).
- Add optimistic backoff + jitter to prefill writers to reduce write conflicts.
- Improve KV store CAS path to better handle hot-write bursts (sharding or per-key locks).

Instrumentation / next steps (concrete):
- [ ] Enable verbose kv-store logging on leader for one hour during next ramp window (JIRA-RT-4123). Watch for write-conflict rates, include X-Trace ids. (Jared)
- [ ] Run controlled experiment: 4 runs: (window=40,limit=24), (40,48), (20,24), (20,48) and collect p95/p99 + kv hit-rate + prefill_initiated counters. (me)
- [ ] Implement quick dedupe layer in batcher for prefill: single-flight per-prefix for 24h trial on canary. (Priya)
- [ ] Add metric: prefill_retries_per_prefix (new exporter) -> helps detect feedback loops. (infra)
- [ ] Post-mortem draft if incident recurs; include timeline + mitigation steps.

Notes / miscellaneous bits:
- Observed a handful of traces where prefill job completed but downstream inference used stale kv-version: commit ordering issues? Might be unrelated but note.
- Slack thread: #runtime-ops has initial alerts (link in linked_artifacts). Use trace tag tr-id for correlation.
- Cost impact: brief drop in throughput -> 6% higher per-token cost for 12m window (rough ballpark)

Scratch commands to re-run later: (keep for myself)
- loadgen --rps 850 --avg-tokens 8 --prefix-heavy true --duration 1800 --target-pool gpool-s-4 --batcher-window-ms 20
- curl "http://kv-leader.internal/debug/locks" | jq .active_locks
- kubectl -n runtime exec -it batcher-xxx -- /bin/pprof -http=:6060 cpu.pprof

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Are there other pools with similar config changes deployed at the same time? (check cluster-deploy history).
- Is there any network blip to KV store around the times (not observed in infra alerts).
- Are some client patterns (small prefixes repeated) more responsible? Need to add histogram of prefixes per time window.

Low-priority "nice to have":
- Visualization: heatmap of prefix frequency vs kv-hit-rate per minute.
- A synthetic test harness that can quickly vary prefill.concurrent_limit and batch window to show the multi-dimensional surface.

If I get time today: start the 4-run experiment and gather p95/p99 + exporter metrics. Otherwise will schedule with Jared tomorrow morning.

-- Samira

(Version note: This is a personal scratchpad; not polished. If copying into an incident document, remove TODO markers and add timestamps for each mitigation action.)
